title.narrative: Urban waste management and resource utilization in Africa: Practice and experience in Shanghai, China and Lagos, Nigeria

description.narrative: Project Description As the world is rapidly urbanizing, waste generation is concurrently rising at an alarming rate. Globally, over 50% of the population lives in urban areas today. By 2045, the world's urban population will increase by 1.5 to 6 billion (68% of the projected world population). Most of this growth is occurring in Africa and Asia with Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) taking the lead as the world's fastest-urbanizing region. Cities such Cairo in Egypt, Kinshasa in DRCongo and Lagos in Nigeria are expected to be part of the world largest megacities by 2045. China has also experienced rapid urbanization in recent decades. In 1950, only 13% of people in China lived in cities; by 2010, the urban share of the population had grown to 45%; it is projected to reach 60% by 2030. On the one hand, Lagos is set to become the third-largest megacity in Africa by 2050. It is already a megacity, with a population of 15.5 million with a forecast to grow by 82% over the next few decades, to 28.2 million. It has the fourth-highest GDP in Africa and is home to one of the largest and busiest seaports in the continent. Lagos is a major financial centre in Africa and has been deemed the cultural, financial and entertainment capital of Africa. It accounts for around 10% of the total GDP for the country. The fast growth encountered by the city put a strain on services, waste management included. On the other hand, Shanghai as the 3rd most populous city in the world with a current metro population of 29.8 million people after Tokyo in Japan and Dheli in India and is projected to reach over 34 million people by 2050. It is also the largest economic centre and an important international financial center city in China. In 2023, Shanghai achieved a regional gross domestic product (GDP) of 4.72 trillion yuan (USD 649 Billion), and its economic output continued to rank first as a national economic centre city, demonstrating strong economic development momentum. The city has. Invested tremendously to put in place a waste management system to efficiently deal with the generation. With rapid urbanization and economic development which leads to higher waste generation in cities, it is critical that city management plan for growth and provide the basic services, infrastructure, policies and incentives necessary to tackle the higher solid waste generation in there cities. With this background this project aims to improve urban solid waste management through informed decision making backed by effective knowledge and technology transfer. It aim to deliver a knowledge tool that compare the two mega cities i.e Shanghai, China and Lagos, Nigeria approaches to Solid waste management, the project will deliver case studies and experiences from Africa while adopting the already conducted studies on Solid waste management of Shanghai City in China by Tongji University. The project will also deliver critical advocacy and knowledge sharing activities to sensitize urban stakeholders on the lessons learnt and recommendations learnt from the knowledge tool, with Key target audience being Africa’s National and Local Governments. Project Approach The starting point of the delivery of the project will be the delivery of a knowledge tool in terms of a joint Publication with Tongji University that will aim to shade light to the pressing issue of Urban Solid Waste Management in Lagos, Nigeria and Shanghai, China. The development of a Knowledge tool will commence with defining the publication outlines then proceed to data collection and analysis of rapid urbanization trends with focus on select Mega Cities i.e Lagos in Nigeria. Response solutions will be identified. Relevant responses will also be identified from other disciplines such as urban planning and legislation and how they interconnect with Uran Solid waste management in the city. The effectiveness of the city strategies on Solid Waste Management in the short and long term will be assessed. To gather and assess data from Lagos, Nigeria UN-Habitat will contract an expert to support the process which will later inform the preparation of a case study outline of the publication. Once the data collection and case studies compilation is completed a workshop to review the content of case studies and agree on key recommendations of the publication will be held. This workshop will also serve the purpose of learning about Shanghai, China responses to similar circumstances and establishing networks between the experts. After the review and agreement on key recommendations, the project will proceed to compile Knowledge tool which will then be subjected to a validation process then after proceed to finalization and publication. Once the knowledge tool has been published the project will proceed to conduct a dissemination campaign for the publication at important local and international events to encourage uptake of the publication key recommendations and conclusions.
